body:
Why institutional support is needed

A student, farmer, artisan or small business may have valuable knowledge but lack experience in identifying intellectual property, preparing applications, assessing commercial potential or finding a suitable partner. Public institutions and support programmes help connect these activities.

In Gujarat, it is important to distinguish IP facilitation, institutional innovation support, business incubation and the legal authority that grants IP rights. These are related functions but are not performed by one single office.

GUJCOST and the Intellectual Property Facilitation Centre

The Gujarat Council on Science and Technology (GUJCOST) operates under the Government of Gujarat's Department of Science and Technology. Its Intellectual Property Facilitation Centre (IPFC), based at Gandhinagar, supports awareness and facilitation relating to intellectual property.

The IPFC's activities include guidance on patent searching and filing, trademarks, industrial designs, geographical indications and other IP matters. It conducts awareness programmes and offers support to students, researchers, academic institutions, startups, innovators and micro, small and medium enterprises.

The centre also provides guidance for assessing the commercial potential of research and identifying industry partners, possible licensees or investors.

Facilitation is not registration: GUJCOST's IPFC can guide and assist applicants. It does not replace the statutory patent or GI registration authorities.

IP Cells in universities and colleges

GUJCOST supports the establishment of Intellectual Property Cells in educational institutions. An institutional IP Cell provides a first point of contact for students and faculty who develop potentially useful innovations.

Its functions include:

  • Creating awareness about intellectual property among students and teachers.
  • Collecting invention disclosures and conducting preliminary screening.
  • Maintaining records of institutional innovation activities.
  • Connecting the institution with GUJCOST's IPFC for appropriate expert assistance.
  • Encouraging protection and possible commercialisation of suitable research outputs.

An IP Cell is therefore a campus-level unit, whereas the GUJCOST IPFC provides wider facilitation across institutions and other eligible stakeholders.

Student Startup and Innovation Policy 2.0

Gujarat's Student Startup and Innovation Policy (SSIP) 2.0 was introduced in January 2022. Its stated policy period runs from January 2022 to March 2027.

The policy supports student innovation and entrepreneurship through measures such as assistance for proof-of-concept development, prototypes, intellectual property, mentorship, incubation and connections with industry.

A proof of concept is an initial demonstration that an idea may work in practice. A prototype is an early version of a product developed for testing or further improvement. Neither is equivalent to a market-ready product or a granted patent.

i-Hub Gujarat is part of the state's student innovation and startup support ecosystem. It provides a platform for incubation and related startup assistance. The official SSIP portal also identifies the Gujarat Knowledge Society as the nodal agency for policy implementation.

Funding or IP assistance under SSIP 2.0 is subject to its prescribed conditions. For institutional IP support, the institute's or university's SSIP Scrutiny Committee evaluates and approves applications. The existence of a programme does not mean that every proposed invention automatically receives support or registration.

Other Gujarat-relevant institutional examples

The Gujarat National Law University–GUJCOST Centre of Excellence on IPR Laws, Policies and Practices was established in 2014 to support research, training and awareness concerning intellectual property law and policy.

For agricultural and craft GIs, NABARD has supported awareness, documentation and registration-related work. A Press Information Bureau release dated 15 June 2026 specifically described NABARD's support for Jasdan Patari Craft under its Gramya Vikas Nidhi, with facilitation by the Centre for Environment Education. The release also identified earlier support associated with Ajrakh Block Print in Kachchh and Amalsad Chikoo in Navsari.

These activities support producer groups in obtaining recognition and market opportunities. They do not convert NABARD into the authority responsible for granting GI registration.

Applying the institutional roles

Consider a student team in Gujarat that develops a useful agricultural implement. The team may first disclose its work through an institutional IP Cell. GUJCOST's IPFC may help assess possible IP protection, while SSIP-related institutions may support development or incubation. A business may later become a manufacturing or licensing partner.

If a group of artisans instead seeks a GI for an established regional craft, its needs are different. It must document the geographical identity of the goods and pursue registration through the national GI system. Facilitation and financial or documentation support may assist the process, but they do not substitute for statutory registration.

Prelims focus

  • GUJCOST functions under Gujarat's Department of Science and Technology.
  • GUJCOST's Intellectual Property Facilitation Centre is located at Gandhinagar.
  • Institutional IP Cells provide campus-level awareness, invention disclosure and preliminary facilitation.
  • SSIP 2.0 covers the stated period January 2022 to March 2027.
  • Gujarat Knowledge Society is the nodal agency for SSIP 2.0 implementation.
  • Trap: GUJCOST, an IP Cell, SSIP institutions and NABARD do not themselves grant GI registrations.

[Sources: GUJCOST, 'Intellectual Property Facilitation Centre (IPFC)', sections 'Introduction', 'Services Offered' and 'IPR Center of Excellence'; GUJCOST, 'Intellectual Property (IP) Cell', section 'About the Intellectual Property Cell'; GUJCOST, 'IP Commercialisation', sections 'Objectives' and 'Support Available'; Government of Gujarat, SSIP official portal, 'About SSIP 2.0', policy period and implementation arrangements; Press Information Bureau, 'Jasdan Patari Handicraft Receives GI Recognition', 15 June 2026; online sources consulted 14 November 2026.]

pictures.alt: Gujarat organisations provide innovation support, NABARD assists selected rural-product GIs, and the GI Registry in Chennai handles statutory GI registration.
pictures.caption: Different institutions support different stages of innovation and GI protection.

title: Gujarat Institutions Supporting Intellectual Property and Commercialisation

body:
Why intellectual property awareness matters to MSMEs

Micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) play an important role in manufacturing, services, employment and local enterprise. A small business may produce an innovative article, develop a recognisable brand or participate in the production of a registered GI product.

Each situation requires a different understanding of intellectual property. Without adequate awareness, a business may fail to protect an eligible invention, misunderstand the use of a protected geographical name or spend money on an unsuitable form of registration.

MSME Innovative Scheme

The Government of India's MSME Innovative Scheme brings together support relating to incubation, design and intellectual property rights. It operates within the broader MSME Champions framework.

Its IPR component seeks to increase IP awareness, encourage the protection and effective use of innovation, support commercialisation and establish Intellectual Property Facilitation Centres.

The activities include counselling and guidance, assistance with IP-related procedures and reimbursement of eligible registration expenses within prescribed ceilings.

Financial assistance under the IPR component

The official scheme portal and the Ministry's 2022 guidelines specify the following maximum financial assistance under the IPR component. These are scheme ceilings, not automatic payments. Eligibility, supporting documents, approval and applicable scheme conditions determine whether reimbursement is available.

IP registrationMaximum assistance
Foreign patent₹5 lakh
Domestic patent₹1 lakh
Geographical indication₹2 lakh
Industrial design₹15,000
Trademark₹10,000

The programme also provides for grants of up to ₹1 crore for the establishment of eligible IP Facilitation Centres, subject to scheme approval and milestones. This is support to a facilitation centre and must not be confused with reimbursement to an individual enterprise for an IP registration.

For patent, trademark and design reimbursements, the guidelines specify Udyam Registration and other relevant conditions. The GI reimbursement provisions separately recognise eligible representative institutions, associations, non-profit bodies and similar organisations. Consequently, the ₹2 lakh GI ceiling should not be interpreted as an entitlement for every individual seller of a GI product.

Scheme status and cutoff: The amounts above are the maxima stated in the Ministry of MSME's 2022 scheme guidelines and on the MSME Innovative IPR portal consulted on 14 November 2026. They describe available scheme provisions, not the amounts paid to all applicants or the number of registrations achieved.

Choosing the correct type of intellectual property

The central skill in applying this subtopic is to identify what is being protected before choosing an IP instrument.

SituationAppropriate IP conceptReason
Traditional textile linked to a defined Gujarat regionGeographical indicationProtects the recognised origin-linked identity of the goods
Business name distinguishing one producer from othersTrademarkIdentifies the commercial source
New eligible functional invention developed at a universityPatentProtects qualifying technical invention rights
Eligible visual appearance of a manufactured articleIndustrial designProtects specified visual design features
Confidential commercially valuable production knowledgeTrade secret or confidential know-howRelies on maintaining confidentiality and appropriate legal protection

Can one product involve several kinds of IP?

Yes. A producer of an authentic Gujarat GI product may also use a separate commercial trademark. Its packaging may contain eligible artistic expression or design features. Equipment used in production could independently embody patented technology.

These rights remain legally distinct. Ownership of a packaging design does not create a right to use a GI, and a patent on production equipment does not grant permission to misrepresent the geographical origin of the goods.

This is especially important when universities collaborate with local industry. A university may license its patented technology to an eligible business. If that business also produces GI goods, it must independently satisfy the GI requirements for the protected geographical indication.

Applying the rules to common situations

A registered GI and a new application are different

A product may be locally famous or may have a GI application under examination without yet being registered. Its registration status must be checked from the official record for the relevant date. The 31 December 2025 Gujarat list, for example, does not contain later registrations identified during 2026.

One registered proprietor does not imply one producer

A GI may have a representative registered proprietor and several authorised users. The authorised-user system allows eligible producers to use the indication under the applicable conditions.

A GI does not become transferable because it has commercial value

Even when GI products are valuable and successfully marketed, section 24 prohibits assignment and licensing of the registered GI right. The ability to buy and sell genuine products is different from transferring the legal entitlement to produce under the indication.

A university invention and a traditional GI follow different paths

For a university invention, the principal questions concern novelty, applicable rights, ownership, possible licensing and commercial adoption. For a traditional GI, the principal questions concern geographical origin, recognised product characteristics, representative registration and authorised users.

Bringing the Gujarat examples together

Gujarat's GI and innovation ecosystem demonstrates 2 complementary routes to economic value. The first protects established place-linked products, such as Patan Patola, Kutch Ajrakh, Gir Kesar Mango and Bhalia Wheat. The second helps move new research and technology from universities and innovators towards useful application through industry collaboration, incubation and appropriate IP agreements.

Public support can assist both routes. GUJCOST facilitates awareness and IP-related procedures; SSIP 2.0 supports student innovation; NABARD has supported selected GI registration initiatives; and the national MSME Innovative Scheme provides specified IPR support. None of these programmes changes the underlying legal distinction between a GI and a licensable invention.

Prelims focus

  • MSME Innovative combines incubation, design and IPR support.
  • Under its IPR component, the stated GI registration reimbursement ceiling is ₹2 lakh.
  • The stated ceilings are ₹1 lakh for a domestic patent and ₹5 lakh for a foreign patent.
  • GUJCOST IPFC facilitates IP protection and commercialisation; the GI Registry grants GI registrations.
  • GI protection concerns origin-linked goods, while university technology transfer often concerns inventions and know-how.
  • Trap: A patent licence, trademark licence and GI authorised-user registration are not the same legal arrangement.

[Sources: Ministry of MSME, 'MSME Innovative Scheme: Guidelines', 2022, section 4.3, 'Intellectual Property Rights (IPR) Component', printed pp. 14–17; Ministry of MSME, 'MSME Innovative (IPR): About Scheme', sections 'Scheme Objective', 'Activities' and 'Nature of Assistance'; GUJCOST, 'Intellectual Property Facilitation Centre' and 'IP Commercialisation'; WIPO, 'IP Assignment and Licensing'; Geographical Indications of Goods (Registration and Protection) Act, 1999, sections 17, 21 and 24; online sources consulted 14 November 2026.]

pictures.alt: Parallel GI and technology routes reach markets through different IP rights, with Gujarat support institutions and the Section 24 ban on licensing registered GI rights.
pictures.caption: Gujarat's GI products and new technologies create value through different legal routes.
